title: Dispatch: fail closed on jhpt state/expected-result contradictions (attempt 1)
description:
Dispatch child of eshyra-o9bd.19.9 (Transition W7). Read `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.9`
for the parent spec and `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.9.3` for the previous round.
This bead repairs the ONE remaining BLOCKING review finding on PR #515, reviewed
at head `7edcf64e14740ddc03f8aa50b7cf0fc40e1bb781`, profile
`rules-clause-complete`. Read the finding first with
`gh pr view 515 --json comments` (the most recent CHANGES REQUIRED comment).

ACCEPTED AND CLOSED — do not redo, do not "improve": the selected-interpretation
chain, the currency gate, the executions split, and the campaign-rule route
mapping. CI is green at the reviewed head; do not chase CI.

The reviewer classifies this repair as NON-MATERIAL provided it stays confined to
correcting P7's no-ruling representation plus fail-closed validation and tests,
changing no scenario meaning. Staying inside that boundary is worth real care: it
is what lets the next review be bounded fix verification instead of a fresh full
review. Do not refactor anything else.

BRANCH / WORKTREE
Branch `eshyra-o9bd.19.9.4`, worktree `.worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.9.4`, cut from
the parent branch `eshyra-o9bd.19.9` at its current head `c2b66cc` (which already
merged origin/main for PR #516). Work only inside that worktree;
`cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` after entering it.

The supervisor independently confirmed every claim below against the code before
filing this bead. They are real; implement rather than re-arguing, but verify
each mechanism yourself as you fix it.

=== THE DEFECT ===

Field 4 (`campaignRuleState`, active rules/rulings or explicit none) and field 12
(`expectedCampaignRuleOrRulingState`, which rules/rulings must appear) can
contradict each other, and the validator does not stop it. W8 needs both as a
machine-readable oracle; a generic consumer must not need prose interpretation or
P7-specific logic to decide whether a ruling exists.

P7's `without-active-ruling` execution is the concrete instance and, verified by
sweeping all twelve fixtures, the ONLY one:

  campaignRuleState:                    none(...)          <- says no ruling
  expectedRouteClasses:                 no campaign-ruling  <- correct
  expectedCampaignRuleOrRulingState:    campaign-rule-cases containing a case
                                        with ruleKind: 'ruling' whose prose
                                        explains that no ruling was supplied

Field 12 structurally asserts a ruling case while field 4 says none. The
unresolved / owner-`campaign-ruling` expectation already belongs in
`expectedAmbiguityState` and in field 4's own none-statement, so field 12 has
nothing left to carry here and should structurally be explicit none.

Confirmed validator gaps, all fail-open:
  - inactive `campaignRuleState` only prohibits the two campaign routes; it does
    NOT require field 12 to be explicit none;
  - active `campaignRuleState` performs no state->expected-case check at all, so
    field 12 may be explicit none;
  - the resolved-ambiguity <-> ruling-selection agreement check only runs when
    field 12 is `campaign-rule-cases`, so replacing field 12 with explicit none
    skips it entirely;
  - `CampaignRuleCase.ruleKind` is optional, so a case can evade the
    `CAMPAIGN_RULE_ROUTE_BY_KIND` mapping altogether;
  - a `ruling` case is not required to carry its route-evidence identity.

Generalized consequences the reviewer named, both currently accepted by the
validator: P7 with active ruling state and a `campaign-ruling` route but field 12
replaced by explicit none; and P10 with active house-rule state and its
`campaign-rule` route but field 12 replaced by explicit none. P10 is correct
today, but nothing protects that correctness.

=== REQUIRED REPAIR ===

1. P7 `without-active-ruling`: `expectedCampaignRuleOrRulingState` becomes
   explicit `none(...)` with a statement saying no ruling is active and that the
   unresolved state and its `campaign-ruling` owner are carried by the ambiguity
   state. Do not lose the owner fact — confirm it remains visible in
   `expectedAmbiguityState` and/or field 4's none-statement, and strengthen the
   ambiguity statement if it does not already say it. Nothing else about this
   execution changes: still unresolved, still both published interpretations,
   still no `campaign-ruling` route, still no selected interpretation, still
   capability `blocked`.

2. Make the state/result invariants fail closed in `validateDiagnosticCorpus`,
   as generic rules (no probe-specific branches):
   - inactive `campaignRuleState` (kind none) REQUIRES field 12 to be explicit
     none, AND neither `campaign-rule` nor `campaign-ruling` may appear in the
     routes (keep the existing route prohibition);
   - active `campaignRuleState` REQUIRES field 12 to be `campaign-rule-cases`
     with at least one case — explicit none is rejected;
   - every case in an active field 12 MUST declare `ruleKind`, so no case can
     evade the route mapping;
   - a case with `ruleKind: 'ruling'` MUST carry the design's route-evidence
     identity: ruling identity, ambiguity id, and selected interpretation id;
   - PRESERVE the existing resolved-ambiguity <-> ruling-selection agreement
     check, and make sure it can no longer be skipped by swapping field 12 to
     explicit none (the new active-state rule should make that unreachable, but
     confirm it rather than assuming).

3. Keep the `DiagnosticFixture` type, `FIXTURE_KEYS`, `EXECUTION_KEYS`, and the
   validation in sync. If you make a `CampaignRuleCase` field required in a
   context, express that in validation — the optional-in-type / required-in-
   context split is fine, but the validator is the enforcement layer because
   `test/**` is outside `tsc --build`.

Adversarial tests required (add to the existing mutation test):
  - P7 no-ruling execution mutated to carry a `campaign-rule-cases` field 12
    (i.e. today's shape) -> rejected;
  - P7 active-ruling execution with field 12 replaced by explicit none ->
    rejected;
  - P10 active house-rule state with field 12 replaced by explicit none ->
    rejected;
  - a case with `ruleKind` removed -> rejected;
  - a `ruling` case missing its ruling identity / ambiguity id / selected
    interpretation id -> rejected.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===
- Test-only. No production code, generated pack data, or schema changes.
- NON-MATERIAL boundary: correct P7's no-ruling representation and add
  fail-closed validation plus tests. Change no other fixture's meaning, and do
  not restructure the contract beyond what these invariants need.
- P7 and P10 remain consumers of the eshyra-jhpt oracle; no discovery-owned
  ruling store, schema, resolver, or lifecycle.
- No fixture asserts a count of records; no coverage/readiness/completeness
  figure over the corpus.
- Every fixture keeps its bounded-evidence statement and `verifiedAtCommit`.
- Do not weaken or edit any existing test or audit expectation.

=== NON-VACUITY IS PART OF THE JOB ===
A previous round shipped a mutation test that was vacuous: it had to satisfy an
upstream invariant to construct its input, so an earlier check rejected it and
the guard under test never ran — the test passed identically with that guard
disabled. For EACH new rule you add: disable that rule alone, confirm the
matching mutation test FAILS, restore, and report what you observed. If a
mutation cannot isolate its guard because validation rejects the input earlier,
say so and unit-test the guard directly instead of pretending the composed case
proves it.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root, BEFORE committing (it rewrites
files). Expected: all non-skipped tests pass; documented skips are the live-API
integration tests and the Dolt-gated checkpoint tests. The one acceptable Biome
finding is the pre-existing biome.json schema-version info.
acceptance_criteria: P7's without-active-ruling execution declares expectedCampaignRuleOrRulingState as explicit none while retaining the unresolved state, both published interpretations, no campaign-ruling route, no selected interpretation, and blocked capability; the campaign-ruling owner fact remains visible. validateDiagnosticCorpus fails closed generically: inactive campaignRuleState requires explicit-none field 12 and forbids both campaign routes; active campaignRuleState requires non-empty campaign-rule-cases; every active case declares ruleKind; a ruling case carries ruling identity, ambiguity id, and selected interpretation id; the resolved-ambiguity/ruling-selection agreement check remains and cannot be skipped. Adversarial tests reject P7 no-state-with-ruling-case, P7 active-state-with-explicit-none, P10 active-state-with-explicit-none, a case missing ruleKind, and a ruling case missing route-evidence identity. Per-rule non-vacuity demonstrated and reported. No production code, generated pack data, or schema changes; no other fixture meaning changed. npm run verify:worktree passes.
